chapter_theme: Natrinai 281 to 300: the friend's voice again leads, pressing for marriage with the hidden lover listening, fearing the veri rite and the mother's watch, and refusing the night visit; men are torn between work and the woman, a mother curses the mother of the youth who took her daughter, a courtesan mocks the husband as a bee, and puram fame (Malaiyan's cattle raids at Mullur, Thazhumban's Unur, Chezhiyan's Koodal, the Cholas' Kazhar) is turned into the measure of akam loss.

281.reading: The woman tells her friend that their lover has no love: on this rain-soaked midnight the crows that live on offerings hang dripping on the wind-beaten branch, thinking of the great meat-and-rice offerings the Cholas take at Kazhar, while he, who knows that even with him beside us we lie sleepless and wretched in the cold, has left us to it.
281.nuance: The crows endure the wet night on the memory of a feast; the woman endures it on the memory of the man. Line 8 (தாம் நம் உழையராகவும்) can also be read of the crows (though they are near us) rather than of the lover, which changes who is beside her.

colophon.thurai: வன்பொறை எதிர் அழிந்த தலைமகள் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது ஆற்றாள் எனக் கவன்ற தோழி தலைமகட்கு உரைத்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the lover's absence and the charge that he is without love decide separation

occasion.words: வன்பொறை எதிர் அழிந்த தலைமகள் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது
ஆற்றாள் எனக் கவன்ற தோழி தலைமகட்கு உரைத்ததூஉம் ஆம்

iraicchi.act: the crows hang on the dripping branch through the rainy night, sustained only by thinking of the feast to come
iraicchi.sense: she too lies awake through the cold night living on the thought of what she longs for, and he who knows it is not with her

282.reading: With the man listening, the friend says the girl's bangles slip, the lines of her waist fade and her forehead pales with a sickness her lover gave, which the old diviner with his possession-beans will explain without knowing; it would be fine indeed if his words could ease their bond with the man of the hill where the smoke of agil and brush a hunter burns hides the slope like drifting cloud.
282.nuance: The closing image is apt to the friend's purpose: a fragrant smoke that hides the hillside as cloud does, as their love has been hidden, though its scent now spreads; it has one match, not the two that ullurai needs.

colophon.thurai: சிறைப்புறமாகத் தோழி செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇ வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: the hunter burning agil on the hill slope and the diviner's rite fix kurinji

comparisons.tenor: the smoke of burnt agil and brush hiding the slope

283.reading: The friend asks the lord of the shore, where bright-browed girls pick fragrant neythal flowers like eyes from the backwater to deck their little striped sand-houses, whether it is right that the girl's long-admired beauty should waste away so, for those who trusted his word, truer than the sun that rises over the sea and is worshipped by many.
283.nuance: The praise is the reproach: by setting his word above the sun that all trust, the friend makes any delay in marrying a breach of something public.

colophon.thurai: பகற்குறி வந்த தலைமகனைத் தோழி வரைவு கடாயது. கடிநகர் புக்க தோழி பிற்றை ஞான்று வேறுபடாது ஆற்றினாய் என்று சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: backwater, neythal flowers and the shore lord fix neythal

comparisons.vehicle: பலர் தொழத் தோன்றி ஏமுற விளங்கிய சுடரினும்
comparisons.tenor: the man's word, truer than the sun

occasion.words: பகற்குறி வந்த தலைமகனைத் தோழி வரைவு கடாயது
கடிநகர் புக்க தோழி பிற்றை ஞான்று வேறுபடாது ஆற்றினாய் என்று சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

284.reading: Away on work not yet done, the man says his heart urges him to go to the woman of the dark hanging hair and flower-coloured kohl eyes and end its pain, while his reason, weighing the outcome, says that leaving a task unfinished brings ignorance and disgrace and bids him not hurry at all; caught between them, he asks whether his aching body will perish like an old frayed rope that two tuskers with gleaming tusks have seized at either end.
284.nuance: The heart and the reason are both given speech (என்னும், twice), so the poem is a debate in which the body is the only loser; the poet's name is taken from the rope.

colophon.thurai: பொருள் முடியாநின்ற தலைமகன் ஆற்றானாகிச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the man held away by unfinished work longs to go back: separation

comparisons.vehicle: போதின் நிறம் பெறும் ஈர் இதழ்ப் பொலிந்த உண்கண்
ஒளிறு ஏந்து மருப்பின் களிறு மாறு பற்றிய தேய்புரிப் பழங் கயிறு
comparisons.tenor: his body pulled between heart and reason

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: he reports the speech of his heart and of his reason to himself

285.reading: With the man listening, the friend tells the girl that the friendship of the hill lord, where a hunter who has shot a porcupine with his bow goes home to his stilted hut delighted, his house dog romping beside the kill, is good for them indeed: not only does he come in the dead of night when the snake hunts its prey, but, never kept away by the neighbours' talk, he now comes by day to the cleared field as well.
285.nuance: The praise is ironic: coming by night and by day has made the talk loud, and the friend's real word is that the affair can no longer stay hidden. The hunter carrying his catch home is the act the man has not yet done.

colophon.thurai: தோழி சிறைப்புறமாகத் தலைமகட்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய் தலைமகன் கேட்ப அம்பலும் அலரும் ஆயிற்று என்று சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the hill hunter, the porcupine and the hill lord fix kurinji

iraicchi.act: the hunter brings his kill home to his own hut and household in open delight
iraicchi.sense: the man should likewise take what he has won home openly, instead of coming to her by night and by day

286.reading: The friend tells the grieving girl, who sobs again and again with her jewels slipping, 'he has surely gone over the bare hills where the kumizh flower, like a bright swinging earring in a slit lobe, streaks the rock floor; let my life go', to stop lamenting: if she thinks about it, he went to win the advancement of his friends and to come back so that her shoulders regain their beauty.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடை மெலிந்த தலைமகளைத் தோழி வற்புறுத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the wasteland kumizh on the bare rock hills and the lover's going fix paalai

287.reading: The girl, unable to bear the tightened watch, says that since the day the lord of the cold shore of neythal-leaved backwaters came, driven by great love and unafraid of the dread crocodile, like a noble warrior who says 'we hold the good fort' while a king with green-eyed elephants besieges its sky-high wall, her heart has not left him, and whenever in the dead of night she hears a bird's cry she takes it for the clear chime of his chariot bell and forgets sleep while the whole town sleeps.
287.nuance: The siege simile is grammatically the man's (fearless before the crocodile), but the colophon's watch (காப்பு மிகுதி) lets it fall also on her: a heart besieged by her household that still says 'we hold it'.

colophon.thurai: காப்பு மிகுதிக்கண் ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகள் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: backwater, neythal and the shore lord fix neythal

comparisons.vehicle: பைங் கண் யானை வேந்து புறத்து இறுத்த நல் எயிலுடையோர் உடையம் என்னும் பெருந் தகை மறவன்
comparisons.tenor: the shore lord who fears no crocodile

288.reading: With the man listening, the friend tells the girl that, seeing the pallor spread on her forehead since the lord of the hill went away, the hill where a plumed peacock dances with its hen on a high branch of the waterfall-loud, god-haunted peak to take the young sun, their mother has set paddy before the red old women to consult the diviner; and if she asks, will the diviner not say that the girl went to the hill to scare small parrots from the red millet and that great Vel has seized her?
288.nuance: The diviner's verdict names the true place (the millet field) and the wrong cause (the god), so the friend's fear is also a hint to the listener that the truth is half out.

colophon.thurai: தோழி சிறைப்புறமாகத் தலைமகட்கு உரைப்பாளாய் வெறி அறிவுறீஇ வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: peacock, millet and the hill lord fix kurinji

iraicchi.act: the peacock dances together with its hen on the high branch in the morning sun
iraicchi.sense: the creatures of his own hill keep company with their mates while he has gone away and left her to pale

289.reading: The woman tells her friend that her lover would not shift from a word he had spoken even if the earth shifted from its place, yet the sky has scooped up the sea, darkened thickly, poured heavy rain and sounded its harsh voice again and again, and has made the rainy season here beside her; meanwhile, like the great log the herdsmen of the scrub set burning at night, she is unpitied and wretched.
289.nuance: She does not doubt his word; the season he named has simply arrived without him, so the burning log, lit and left by others to burn down alone, carries the whole of her complaint.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடைப் பருவம் கண்டு சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the rains come and herdsmen of the scrub fix mullai

comparisons.vehicle: கொல்லைக் கோவலர் எல்லி மாட்டிய பெரு மர ஒடியல்

290.reading: Aiming her words at the wife through the dancing woman, the courtesan says to her: if you want the friendship of the lord of the town where an old slow-footed bull grazes on the leftovers of the fresh white field lilies that a cow with a new calf has eaten, do not take my word for it, sharp-toothed one: you are a great beauty, but he, they say, is a bee that comes at midnight to the deep pond and sucks the cool fragrant new flowers; they do not call him a man.
290.nuance: The courtesan's mockery cuts three ways: at the dancing woman as the new favourite, at the wife as the cow whose leftovers he grazes, and at the man as a bee, not a man.

colophon.thurai: பரத்தை விறலிமேல் வைத்துத் தலைமகளை நெருங்கிச் சொல்லியது பரத்தையிற்பிரிய வாயிலாய்ப் புக்க பாணன் கேட்ப தோழி சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: field lilies, the buffalo-bull and the town lord fix marutham

comparisons.vehicle: தண் கமழ் புது மலர் ஊதும் வண்டு

thurai_akam.speaker: parathai

occasion.words: பரத்தை விறலிமேல் வைத்துத் தலைமகளை நெருங்கிச் சொல்லியது

thurai_akam.note: the words are aimed at the wife through the dancing woman

occasion.words: வாயிலாய்ப் புக்க பாணன் கேட்ப தோழி சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

ullurai.tenor: the husband, who after his wife has borne a son grazes on what other flowers remain

pairs.situation: the wife who has newly borne his son

pairs.scene: தின்ற மிச்சில் ஓய்நடை முது பகடு ஆரும்
pairs.situation: the ageing husband feeding on leftovers, the women beyond his house
the new young women he takes up

ullurai.speaker_fit: the courtesan, not bound to the heroine's world, may use any thing, and the bull at the field is of her own marutham town (porul 7.29)

291.reading: The friend, knowing the wife's mind, tells the bard who came as the man's go-between to tell the lord of the cool sea shore exactly what he has seen: where the water has drawn back from the thick mire, a flock of herons that came to eat fat oily-headed fish climbs the heaped white sand and shines like the bright array of kings' armies; and her beauty is ruined like the owners of the many cows the king of great dark Mullur drove off at nightfall, riding his horse.
291.nuance: The herons that feast where the water has left mirror a man who has taken his pleasure and gone; the closing simile takes the side of the herd-owners, not of the raiding king the puram poets praise.

colophon.thurai: வாயிலாகப் புக்க பாணற்குத் தோழி தலைமகளது குறிப்பு அறிந்து நெருங்கிச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: herons on the sea shore and the shore lord fix neythal

comparisons.tenor: the flock of herons on the white sand

comparisons.vehicle: மா ஊர்ந்து எல்லித் தரீஇய இன நிரைப் பல் ஆன் கிழவரின்

occasion.words: வாயிலாகப் புக்க பாணற்குத் தோழி தலைமகளது குறிப்பு அறிந்து நெருங்கிச் சொல்லியது

ullurai.tenor: the man who took his pleasure of her and went

pairs.scene: நீர் பெயர்ந்து மாறிய செறி சேற்று அள்ளல்
pairs.situation: the love that has drained away and left her stranded

pairs.scene: நெய்த் தலைக் கொழு மீன் அருந்த இனக் குருகு
pairs.situation: he who fed on her beauty and keeps company with others

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses herons and fish of the neythal shore in a neythal poem (porul 7.27)

292.reading: The friend tells the man that he does not think of the forest where honey-gatherers pull down and break the fragrant green-leaved tamaala creeper wound round the swaying branch of tall cool sandal, nor heed the crocodile that moves in the hard whirlpools of the black-rock forest stream whose deep bank, broken where elephants fought, glitters with crystal and red gold; if he comes by night in this thick dark dew, she will not live.
292.nuance: Traditionally the creeper torn from the sandal by honey-takers is the girl harmed by the man's pleasure; the poem gives no second correspondence, so it stays scene.

colophon.thurai: இரவுக்குறி மறுத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: forest stream, night visit and dense dew fix kurinji

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no speaker; the friend refuses for the girl

293.reading: The mother, bewildered in her house, wishes that the mother who bore the cruel young man, who won her thick-haired daughter with his words and resolved to take her away, may, whenever she sees the bright-eyed band of girls in the wide common of the ancient town of old renown, where the festival has begun and the old potter in his nochchi garland, toddy of the offering in hand, cries out the offerings, tremble with as great an anguish as hers.
293.nuance: The curse falls not on the young man but on his mother, the one person whose loss would match her own; the festival crowd of girls is where the absent daughter would have been.

colophon.thurai: தாய் மனை மருண்டு சொல்லியது அவரிடத்தாரைக் கண்டு சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the daughter's going with her lover is the uri of paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: no addressee: she speaks to herself

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: to people of the young man's side

294.reading: The friend, entering the wedding house and seeing the bride's beauty, says it is no illusion: just as the sky bore both fire and wind, so the open chest of the lord of the shining hill, whose slopes are fragrant with kaanthal whose red-sided buds have opened like the tusk of an elephant killed by an old enemy in the bamboo-thick rock clefts, has become both the sickness and the joy.
294.nuance: The cosmological simile (the sky as the source of both fire and wind) makes the cure and the sickness one origin, now that the marriage has turned the one into the other.

colophon.thurai: மணமனையுள் புக்க தோழி தலைமகளது கவின் கண்டு சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: kaanthal on the hill slope and the hill lord fix kurinji

comparisons.tenor: the man's chest, the source of her sickness and her joy

occasion.words: மணமனையுள் புக்க தோழி தலைமகளது கவின் கண்டு சொல்லியது

295.reading: The friend, with the man able to hear, says that the girl's long dark hair, spoiled at the back like valli creeper crushed on a broken slope, has set her playmates grieving and her mother knowing, and the mother has laid a hard watch on her; so, at our father's great port where ships of many tasks come wind-driven from many lands, our young beauty, like the toddy jar at a noisy feast, will be left behind the house door while we go on and grow old.
295.nuance: The toddy jar is set out for a crowd and emptied by others; the friend's image warns that beauty kept indoors under guard is spent with no one to enjoy it.

colophon.thurai: தோழி செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇ வரைவு கடாயது சிறைப்புறமும் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: ships at the great port fix the shore

296.reading: Told by her friend that he is leaving, the woman asks what will become of her: even in the rare season when the parted grieve, when the kondrai's tube-podded hanging clusters bloom grandly on the lone rock like the gold forehead-plate on the spotted face of a king's war elephant, they say her lover will hurry off with a heart set only on his work, and they say she will stay behind, suffering in grief.
296.nuance: The repeated என்ப (they say) twice keeps the news at second hand, so her question is also a refusal to take it as settled.

colophon.thurai: தோழியால் பிரிவு உணர்த்தப்பட்ட தலைமகள் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the lover's leaving decides separation, though the flowering is of the rains

comparisons.vehicle: மன்னர் வினை வல் யானைப் புகர் முகத்து அணிந்த பொன் செய் ஓடைப் புனை நலம்

297.reading: With the man listening, the friend tells the girl that she leaves her milk in its gold bowl, does not stir her red feet, quarrels with her fine bed, wears a joyless look as if joyful, and never asks herself why: the sign showing in her is very plain, and the mother, seeing that the lord of the land where the spotted-legged jungle fowl, sated on fallen buds, sleeps in the ripe pepper vines, came softly and won her heart, will be troubled, and has already held her close without a doubt.
297.nuance: The friend's list of symptoms is aimed at the hidden listener as much as at the girl; the last lines are hard and can also be read as the mother's suspicion rather than her embrace.

colophon.thurai: தோழி சிறைப்புறமாகத் தலைமகட்கு உரைப்பாளாய் தலைமகன் கேட்பச் சொல்லி யது தோழி தலைமகளை அறத்தொடுநிலை வலிப்பித்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the jungle fowl in the pepper vines of the hill lord's land fix kurinji

298.reading: Having been urged by the friend to go for wealth and then come back to the woman, the man tells his heart that it holds to neither side: it thinks of the many great hills of the fearful forked wasteland, where fierce-eyed men with red arrows fitted watch for travellers and the male vulture, hearing the slack-mouthed drum, goes back to its flock, and it looks at her bamboo-smooth shoulders painted with sugarcane; can it both embrace the great mountains and keep its gaze on her hair, fragrant with dark flowers like the rare buds of Koodal of Chezhiyan of the golden chariot?
298.nuance: The man stays: the colophon calls it செலவு அழுங்கியது. The closing lines are hard; the reading of Koodal's flower as the measure of her hair is a guess.

colophon.thurai: தோழியால் பொருள் வலிப்பித்துத் தலைமகளை எய்தி ஆற்றாதாய நெஞ்சினை நெருங் கிச் சொல்லி தலைமகன் செலவு அழுங்கியது

thinai_evidence.note: the robber-held wasteland forks fix paalai

299.reading: With the man listening, the friend says that even if the lovely little village, where the strong west wind shakes the great white thazhai flower, loosened from its tight bonds like the broken tusk of a fearsome elephant, and spreads its fine pollen on the sand-play of the jewelled girls, should grieve, they had known that without him they would be nothing, before ever they laughed with the lord of the shore of the dense sea where full waves rise in spray, struck by wind, like cotton beaten by a bow.
299.nuance: The syntax of lines 5 to 9 is loose; the friend seems to say the girl went into the affair knowing its cost, which makes the man's delay the only thing left to answer for.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறமாகச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: thazhai flowers and the shore lord fix neythal

300.reading: The friend tells the lord of the town of the cool ford, where the water lily, swaying under a strong wind, bows to the lotus as the tender attendants bow with joined hands to an angry princess, that a man has decked his great chariot as the price of the girl's little bangles, stood it at our front gate and gone; and you too come with your chariot and will not leave, touching our kitchen's palm-leaf screen like the great begging elephant at Unur of Thazhumban of the great scar, chief of the bards' kin whose soft-fibred strings shine as if dripping ghee.
300.nuance: The colophon's note says rival strangers have already offered marriage; the friend uses that chariot at the gate to shame the lover, who comes for scraps like a begging elephant instead of asking for her.

colophon.thurai: வாயில் மறுத்தது வரைவு கடாயதூஉம் ஆம் மாற்றோர் நொதுமலாளர் வரைவின் மேலிட்டு மருதத்துக் களவு

thinai_evidence.note: water lily, lotus and the town lord fix marutham

comparisons.vehicle: சுடர்த் தொடிக் கோமகள் சினந்தென அதன் எதிர் மடத் தகை ஆயம் கைதொழுதாஅங்கு
comparisons.tenor: the water lily bowing to the lotus
the lover hanging about the kitchen

links.note: Kural 612 warns against letting a task die half done; in Natrinai 284 the man's own reason says the same, that leaving work unfinished brings ignorance and disgrace, while his heart urges him home.
links.teaches: The pair shows the Kural's maxim on unfinished work already living inside an akam man as the voice of his reason, and the Natrinai adds what the maxim leaves out: obeying it costs a body torn like a rope between two tuskers.

links.note: Natrinai 284 has the man's body as an old rope pulled at both ends by two tuskers, heart against reason; Kural 1163 has the woman's life as a carrying pole with love and shame hung at its two ends, in a body that cannot bear them.
links.teaches: Set side by side, the two show one figure, a load-bearing cord or pole strained between two claims, serving both the man's conflict of love against duty and the woman's of love against shame, so the tradition pictured a lover's divided mind as a physical strain whatever the second claim was.

links.note: Kapilar in Purananuru 123 praises Malaiyan of Mullur for chariots given while sober, more than the raindrops on Mullur's heights; Kapilar in Natrinai 291 measures a girl's ruined beauty by the herd-owners whose cattle the king of Mullur drove off at nightfall on his horse.
links.teaches: Read together, the same poet's two Mullur poems show the giving king's other face: the wealth praised in puram as countless gifts came partly from night raids on herds, and akam borrows the raid from the side of those who lost everything.

links.note: The bereaved mother in Natrinai 293 wishes that the young man's mother may suffer great anguish like hers (எம்போல் பெரு விதுப்புறுகமாதோ); the mourner of Purananuru 291 wishes the same on the king (என்போற் பெருவிதுப்பு உறுக) whose garland sent the man to his death.
links.teaches: The shared curse formula shows that akam treated a daughter's elopement as a bereavement in the full puram sense: the mother speaks in the words a mourner uses over a warrior's body, aimed at the one who caused the loss.

links.note: Paranar in Purananuru 348 compares a girl to rich Unur of truthful Thazhumban and pictures suitors' chariots in every shade and elephants tied at every place for her; Paranar in Natrinai 300, with strangers' marriage offers in the colophon, has a chariot set at the gate as her bride-price and likens the lover to Unur's begging elephant at the kitchen.
links.teaches: Holding the two Paranar poems together shows him using Thazhumban's Unur for the same occasion, a girl besieged by suitors with chariots and elephants: in puram the siege threatens the town, in akam the friend turns it into a goad to make the hidden lover ask for her before others do.

links.note: In Akananuru 242 the mother calls the diviner not knowing that the man who chased parrots from the millet with them came to the girl in love; in Natrinai 288 the friend fears the diviner will say the girl went to scare small parrots from the millet and Vel seized her.
links.teaches: Natrinai 288 puts in the diviner's own verdict the very scene Akananuru 242 says the mother does not know, so the pair shows the veri's error lying not in the facts but in the agent: it finds the right place, the millet field, and names the god instead of the man.

links.note: Natrinai 289's woman says her lover would not shift from his word even if the earth shifted, though the promised rains have come without him; Kural 1154's woman asks whether any fault lies with those who believed the assuring words of one who then left.
links.teaches: On the plain reading the two women answer the same broken promise in incompatible ways, one keeping her faith in his word intact and blaming only her unpitied state, the other turning the promise into a charge against him, which marks out the range a waiting woman's speech could take.

links.note: Kural 1156: if he is hard enough to speak of leaving, the hope of his grace is vain; Natrinai 296: told he will go, the woman asks what will become of her, since he leaves with a heart set on work even in the season when the kondrai blooms and the parted grieve.
links.teaches: Kural 1156 finds the man's hardness in the announcement itself, and Natrinai 296 adds a second measure the couplet does not give, the timing: to leave in the very season made for grieving apart shows a heart given wholly to work.

links.note: Kural 1102: the jewelled woman is herself the cure of the sickness she causes; Natrinai 294: at the wedding, the friend says the man's chest has become both the sickness and the joy, as the sky bore both fire and wind.
links.teaches: The couplet states the paradox as the lover's private discovery in secret union, while Natrinai 294 has the friend confirm it at the wedding, so the pair shows the same claim moving from a lover's wonder to a public fact once marriage makes the cause of the sickness its lawful cure.

links.note: In Natrinai 284 the man already away hears heart and reason argue and fears his body will snap like a rope; in Natrinai 298 the man about to go tells his heart it cannot hold both the hills and her shoulders, and he stays.
links.teaches: Read as a pair, the two poems show the same divided man before and after the journey begins: before it, the heart can still win and the journey is dropped, but once the work is under way reason rules and only the body is left to break.

source_issues: Natrinai colophons give speaker and occasion in prose; thurai_akam follows them, and where they name no addressee (287, 293) the code is pira with a note.
286: the poet's name ends பாலங் கொற்றனார, with the final consonant ர் apparently lost.
297 and 298: the colophon thurai has a word split by a space (சொல்லி யது, நெருங் கிச்); copied as is.
300: the colophon thurai runs on into what looks like an editor's note (மாற்றோர் நொதுமலாளர் வரைவின் மேலிட்டு மருதத்துக் களவு), copied as is.
281 line 8, 297 lines 10-11 and 298 lines 10-12: the syntax is hard and the readings given are marked uncertain.
Inferred thinai agrees with the colophon for all twenty poems.
